bank.name: Battles of Islam (Ghazwat)
bank.subject: Islamic Studies
bank.description: Key battles of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and the early Islamic period.

questions.prompt: How many Muslims fought in the Battle of Badr?
questions.explanation: About 313 Muslims fought at Badr against a Quraysh force of about 1,000.

questions.prompt: In which year (AH) was the Battle of Uhud fought?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Uhud was fought in 3 AH (625 CE).

questions.prompt: Which Muslim leader was martyred at the Battle of Uhud?
questions.explanation: Hamza ibn Abdul-Muttalib, the Prophet's uncle, was martyred at Uhud.

questions.prompt: Which battle took place during the time of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and was won through a trench dug around Madinah?
questions.explanation: The Battle of the Trench (Ahzab/Khandaq) in 5 AH was defended using a trench, on the suggestion of Salman al-Farsi.

questions.prompt: The conquest of Makkah took place in which year?
questions.explanation: Makkah was conquered peacefully in 8 AH (630 CE), in Ramadan.

questions.prompt: Which expedition of the Prophet (PBUH) was the last and the largest?
questions.explanation: The Expedition of Tabuk in 9 AH was the last and largest military expedition of the Prophet (PBUH).

questions.prompt: The Battle of Hunain was fought against which tribe?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Hunain in 8 AH was fought against the Hawazin tribe after the conquest of Makkah.

questions.prompt: Who was the commander of the Muslim army at the Battle of Mu'tah?
questions.explanation: Zaid bin Harithah was the first commander at Mu'tah; after his martyrdom, command passed to Ja'far and then Khalid bin Waleed.

questions.prompt: Who killed the great warrior of the Quraysh, Abu Jahl, at the Battle of Badr?
questions.explanation: Abu Jahl was killed at Badr; according to tradition, Muadh bin Amr and Muawwiz bin Afra were instrumental, with the final blow credited to Abdullah bin Masood.

questions.prompt: In which battle did the Muslims use the strategy of archers stationed on a mountain pass?
questions.explanation: At Uhud, the Prophet (PBUH) posted 50 archers on a hill; their early departure changed the course of the battle.

questions.prompt: The Battle of Khaybar was fought against which community?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Khaybar in 7 AH was fought against the Jewish tribes of Khaybar.

questions.prompt: Which verse of the Quran is called the 'Aayat-e-Karima' and was revealed during a battle?
questions.explanation: Aayat-e-Karima (Surah al-Anbiya 21:87, 'La ilaha illa anta subhanaka...') was revealed during the Battle of Badr.

questions.prompt: Who led the Muslim army in the Battle of Yarmuk against the Byzantines during the caliphate of Abu Bakr?
questions.explanation: Khalid bin Waleed commanded the Muslim forces at the Battle of Yarmuk (636 CE) against the Byzantines.

questions.prompt: The Battle of Qadisiyyah was fought against which empire?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Qadisiyyah (637 CE) was fought between the Muslims and the Sassanid Persian Empire, under Saad bin Abi Waqas.

questions.prompt: In which battle was the uncle of the Prophet (PBUH), Abbas, taken prisoner and later embraced Islam?
questions.explanation: Abbas ibn Abdul-Muttalib was among those captured at Badr; he later embraced Islam.

questions.prompt: Which tribe of Madinah betrayed the Muslims and was dealt with after the Battle of the Trench?
questions.explanation: The Banu Qurayzah broke their pact and allied with the enemy during the Battle of the Trench.

questions.prompt: The first Ghazwa (battle) of Islam is which?
questions.explanation: The first ghazwa was the expedition of Waddan (al-Abwa) in 2 AH, though Badr is the first major battle.

questions.prompt: How many Ghazwat (battles led by the Prophet PBUH) are generally recorded?
questions.explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) personally led about 27 ghazwat (expeditions); some accounts say around 29.

questions.prompt: Who was the standard-bearer of the Muslims at the Battle of Badr?
questions.explanation: Mus'ab bin Umair, the first ambassador of Islam, carried the Muslim standard at Badr.

questions.prompt: In which battle did the famous swordsman Ali ibn Abi Talib defeat Amr bin Abd Wudd?
questions.explanation: At the Battle of the Trench, Ali defeated the Quraysh champion Amr bin Abd Wudd.

questions.prompt: The 'Sariyyah' in Islamic terminology refers to which type of expedition?
options: Expedition led by a companion without the Prophet (PBUH)
questions.explanation: Sariyyah is an expedition sent out under a companion's command, whereas ghazwa is one the Prophet (PBUH) led personally.

questions.prompt: Which battle is referred to as 'Yom al-Furqan' (the Day of Criterion) in the Quran?
questions.explanation: The Quran calls the Battle of Badr 'Yawm al-Furqan' (the day of the criterion) — Surah al-Anfal 8:41.

questions.prompt: The Muslim army at Tabuk was the largest yet, numbering about how many?
questions.explanation: The army of Tabuk in 9 AH is said to have numbered about 30,000.

questions.prompt: Who was the commander of the Quraysh army at Badr?
questions.explanation: Abu Jahl (Amr ibn Hisham) commanded the Quraysh at Badr and was killed.

questions.prompt: How many Quraysh fighters were at the Battle of Badr?
questions.explanation: About 1,000 Quraysh fought against roughly 313 Muslims.

questions.prompt: Who was the first to draw his sword at Badr in the traditional duel?
questions.explanation: The three duels at Badr were fought by Ali, Hamza and Ubaidah (RA) against the Quraysh champions.

questions.prompt: Which verse calls the Muslims at Badr 'a small band' that Allah helped with angels?
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Anfal 8:9 records the Muslims' call for help and the sending of a thousand angels.

questions.prompt: How many Muslims were martyred at Badr?
questions.explanation: Fourteen Muslims were martyred at Badr; 70 Quraysh were killed and 70 captured.

questions.prompt: At Uhud, how many Muslims faced about 3,000 Quraysh?
questions.explanation: About 700 Muslims (after 300 withdrew) faced around 3,000 at Uhud.

questions.prompt: Who commanded the archers at Uhud and was later martyred?
questions.explanation: Abdullah bin Jubair (RA) led the 50 archers; their leaving the post caused the setback at Uhud.

questions.prompt: The treaty at Hudaibiyah was negotiated on behalf of the Quraysh by?
questions.explanation: Suhail bin Amr negotiated for the Quraysh; the treaty was signed in 6 AH.

questions.prompt: Which Surah is called the 'Surah of Victory' (Al-Fath) and was revealed on the return from Hudaibiyah?
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Fath (48) was revealed after the Treaty of Hudaibiyah, calling it a manifest victory.

questions.prompt: Which year is known as the 'Year of Delegations' (Aam-ul-Wufud)?
questions.explanation: In 9 AH delegations from across Arabia accepted Islam after the conquest of Makkah.

questions.prompt: The 'Bai'at-e-Rizwan' (Pledge of Ridwan) was taken under which tree before which event?
options: Before Hudaibiyah, pledging to fight the Quraysh
questions.explanation: Under the tree at Hudaibiyah, the companions pledged loyalty, praised in the Quran (48:18).

questions.prompt: At the conquest of Makkah, the Prophet (PBUH) entered the city from which direction?
options: From the upper (north) side via Kada
questions.explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) entered from the north (Kada) at the head of about 10,000 men.

questions.prompt: How many Muslims entered Makkah at its conquest?
questions.explanation: Roughly 10,000 Muslims marched on Makkah in 8 AH (630 CE).

questions.prompt: What did the Prophet (PBUH) do with the idols in the Kaaba at the conquest of Makkah?
questions.explanation: He destroyed the idols, reciting 'Truth has come and falsehood has vanished' (17:81).

questions.prompt: What was the general amnesty granted at the conquest of Makkah called?
questions.explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) declared amnesty: 'Go, for you are free' — a hallmark of his mercy.

questions.prompt: Who had broken the pact of Hudaibiyah, prompting the conquest of Makkah?
options: The Banu Bakr, allied with Quraysh, against Khuza'a
questions.explanation: The Quraysh-allied Banu Bakr attacked Khuza'a, breaking the treaty and triggering the conquest.

questions.prompt: Which companion guarded the entrance of the cave of Thawr during the Hijrah?
options: Asma bint Abu Bakr brought food; no one guarded the cave
questions.explanation: Abu Bakr's daughter Asma carried provisions, and Abdullah bin Abu Bakr brought news during the three days.

questions.prompt: The spider's web at the Cave of Thawr is associated with which event?
options: The Hijrah, protecting the Prophet (PBUH) and Abu Bakr
questions.explanation: A spider wove its web and a bird nested at the cave entrance, leading pursuers to pass by.

questions.prompt: Which expedition resulted in the 'Sariyyah of Nakhla', the first booty of the Muslims?
options: The expedition led by Abdullah bin Jahsh
questions.explanation: Abdullah bin Jahsh led the Nakhla patrol (2 AH) which captured booty — the first for the Muslims.

questions.prompt: The Battle of the Camel (Jamal) in 656 CE was fought between?
options: Ali (RA) and forces of Aisha (RA), Talha and Zubair
Abu Bakr and the Ridda tribes
questions.explanation: The Battle of Jamal pitted Ali's (RA) forces against those seeking justice for Uthman's (RA) death.

questions.prompt: The Battle of Siffin (657 CE) was fought between?
questions.explanation: Siffin was fought between Ali's (RA) forces and Muawiyah's (RA), ending in arbitration.

questions.prompt: Who seceded from Ali's (RA) camp after Siffin, forming the Kharijites?
options: A group rejecting arbitration, later killed at Nahrawan
questions.explanation: The Kharijites rejected the arbitration at Siffin; Ali (RA) defeated them at Nahrawan in 658.

questions.prompt: Ali (RA) was martyred in 661 CE by whom?
options: A Kharijite named Abd al-Rahman ibn Muljam
questions.explanation: Ali (RA) was struck by Ibn Muljam while praying at Kufa in 40 AH.

questions.prompt: The Battle of Karbala (680 CE) resulted in the martyrdom of whom?
options: Husain ibn Ali (RA) and his family and companions
questions.explanation: Husain ibn Ali (RA) and his companions were martyred at Karbala by Yazid's forces.

questions.prompt: In which year did the Battle of Karbala take place?
questions.explanation: Karbala occurred on 10 Muharram 61 AH (10 October 680 CE).

questions.prompt: The incident of the 'Ashab-ul-Ukhdud' (People of the Trench) is mentioned in which Surah?
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Buruj (85) narrates the believers thrown into a trench of fire.

questions.prompt: The Muslim army at the Battle of Mu'tah numbered about?
questions.explanation: About 3,000 Muslims fought a much larger Byzantine-Arab force at Mu'tah in 8 AH.

questions.prompt: Who was the third commander appointed at Mu'tah after Ja'far's martyrdom?
questions.explanation: After Zaid and Ja'far fell, command passed to Abdullah bin Rawaha, then to Khalid bin Waleed.

questions.prompt: How many Muslims participated in the Battle of Badr?
questions.explanation: Around 313 Muslims fought at Badr.

questions.prompt: Which battle is called 'Yaum-ul-Furqan' (the day of distinction)?
questions.explanation: Badr is called Yaum-ul-Furqan.

questions.prompt: At which battle was the Prophet (PBUH) wounded?
questions.explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) was wounded at Uhud.

questions.prompt: Who was the chief of the archers at Uhud who left their post?
questions.explanation: Abdullah bin Jubair led the archers who abandoned their position.

questions.prompt: The Battle of Khandaq is also known as:
questions.explanation: Khandaq means trench.

questions.prompt: The Battle of Mu'tah was fought against which empire?
questions.explanation: Mu'tah was fought against Byzantine forces.

questions.prompt: Who took the flag at Mu'tah after Zaid bin Haritha fell?
questions.explanation: Ja'far took command and fell next.

questions.prompt: Which year is known as the 'Year of Grief' (Aam-ul-Huzn)?
questions.explanation: 619 CE, the year Khadijah and Abu Talib died.

questions.prompt: The Battle of Hunain took place in which year?
questions.explanation: Hunain occurred in 8 AH after the Conquest of Makkah.

questions.prompt: Which battle was fought without a single arrow being fired by the Muslims?
questions.explanation: Khandaq was won through siege tactics without direct battle.

questions.prompt: The 'Expedition of Tabuk' was the last expedition led by the Prophet (PBUH). In which year?
questions.explanation: Tabuk occurred in 9 AH.

questions.prompt: Who was killed by the Prophet's (PBUH) companion at Badr among the idolaters?
questions.explanation: Abu Jahl (Amr bin Hisham) fell at Badr.

questions.prompt: The Quranic surah that mentions the Battle of Badr is:
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Anfal discusses the Battle of Badr.

questions.prompt: Who was the general of the Quraysh army at Uhud?
questions.explanation: Abu Sufyan led the Quraysh at Uhud.

questions.prompt: The 'Battle of Bani Mustaliq' is also known as:
questions.explanation: The expedition against Bani Mustaliq is the Muraisi campaign.

questions.prompt: Which treaty allowed Muslims to perform Umrah the following year?
questions.explanation: Hudaibiya permitted Umrah the next year.

questions.prompt: The Muslims' first naval expedition under Islam was led by:
questions.explanation: The first naval campaign occurred during Umar's reign under Muawiyah.

questions.prompt: The Battle of Badr took place near which location?
options: The wells of Badr, south of Madinah
questions.explanation: Badr was fought near the wells of Badr, about 150 km south of Madinah.

questions.prompt: Which companion shielded the Prophet (PBUH) with his body at Uhud?
questions.explanation: Talha (RA) protected the Prophet (PBUH) at Uhud and was praised for it.

questions.prompt: How many Muslims were martyred at the Battle of Uhud?
questions.explanation: Around seventy Muslims were martyred at Uhud, including Hamza (RA).

questions.prompt: The incident of the slander (Ifk) is associated with which expedition?
questions.explanation: The slander against Aisha (RA) occurred on the return from the Muraisi expedition.

questions.prompt: The Prophet (PBUH) gave the flag to whom on the day the fort of Khaybar was conquered?
questions.explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) gave the standard to Ali (RA), who conquered the Khaybar fort.

questions.prompt: The expedition of Tabuk was mounted in response to the threat of which empire?
questions.explanation: Tabuk was prepared against the rumoured Byzantine advance on the northern border.

questions.prompt: Who was left in charge of Madinah during the expedition of Tabuk?
questions.explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) left Ali (RA) to govern Madinah during Tabuk.

questions.prompt: Which three companions were left behind at Tabuk and are mentioned in Surah At-Tawbah?
options: Ka'b bin Malik, Murara bin Rabi' and Hilal bin Umayyah
questions.explanation: The repentance of these three is recorded in Surah At-Tawbah.

questions.prompt: The Muslim army at the Battle of Hunain numbered about?
questions.explanation: The Muslims were about 12,000 at Hunain, many of them new converts.

questions.prompt: Who led the Hawazin tribe at the Battle of Hunain?
questions.explanation: Malik bin Awf al-Nasri commanded the Hawazin at Hunain.

questions.prompt: At Hunain, with which words did the Prophet (PBUH) rally the retreating Muslims?
options: I am the Prophet; no lie (Ana al-Nabi la kadhib)
questions.explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) cried 'I am the Prophet, no lie; I am the son of Abdul-Muttalib'.

questions.prompt: Which battle is described in Surah Al-Ahzab?
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Ahzab (33) recounts the Battle of the Trench.

questions.prompt: Which surah was revealed shortly after the Conquest of Makkah?
questions.explanation: Surah An-Nasr announced the help of Allah and the victory of Makkah.

questions.prompt: The Battle of Khaybar was fought in which year?
questions.explanation: Khaybar was conquered in 7 AH.

questions.prompt: Uhud is a mountain near which city?
questions.explanation: Mount Uhud lies just north of Madinah.

questions.prompt: At Khaybar, a Jewish woman offered the Prophet (PBUH) what?
questions.explanation: Zainab bint al-Harith offered the Prophet (PBUH) poisoned mutton at Khaybar.

questions.prompt: The Battle of Hunain is mentioned in which surah?
questions.explanation: Surah At-Tawbah (9:25) mentions the day of Hunain.

questions.prompt: The Battle of the Camel took place in which year?
questions.explanation: The Battle of the Camel took place in 36 AH (656 CE).

questions.prompt: What does 'Furqan' mean, as in 'Yawm al-Furqan'?
options: The criterion between truth and falsehood
questions.explanation: Furqan means the standard that distinguishes truth from falsehood.

questions.prompt: After accepting Islam, Khalid bin Waleed (RA) first fought at which battle?
questions.explanation: Khalid bin Waleed (RA) accepted Islam in 8 AH and first fought as a Muslim at Mu'tah.

questions.prompt: The Battle of the Camel was fought near which city?
questions.explanation: The Battle of the Camel took place near Basra.

questions.prompt: The Battle of Siffin was fought near which river?
questions.explanation: Siffin was fought on the banks of the Euphrates.

questions.prompt: Who was the arbiter for Ali (RA) at the arbitration of Siffin?
questions.explanation: Abu Musa al-Ashari (RA) represented Ali (RA) in the arbitration.

questions.prompt: Who was the arbiter for Muawiyah (RA) at the arbitration of Siffin?
questions.explanation: Amr ibn al-Aas (RA) represented Muawiyah (RA).

questions.prompt: The Battle of Nahrawan was fought against whom?
questions.explanation: Ali (RA) defeated the Kharijites at Nahrawan in 38 AH.

questions.prompt: The Battle of Uhud was fought because the Quraysh wanted to avenge?
questions.explanation: The Quraysh marched on Madinah to avenge their losses at Badr.

questions.prompt: How many Muslims participated in digging the trench at Khandaq?
questions.explanation: About three thousand Muslims dug the trench under the Prophet's (PBUH) direction.

questions.prompt: Who were the allies of the Quraysh at the Battle of the Trench?
options: The confederate tribes (Ahzab), including Banu Ghatafan
questions.explanation: The Quraysh joined with the Ghatafan and other tribes to form the confederates (Ahzab).

questions.prompt: At the Battle of the Trench, which Jewish tribe broke its pact during the siege?
questions.explanation: Banu Qurayzah negotiated with the confederates during the siege and were dealt with after.

questions.prompt: Who was the leader of the Muslims' archers who left their post at Uhud?
questions.explanation: Abdullah bin Jubair (RA) commanded the archers; his men abandoned the pass against orders.

questions.prompt: Which battle is called 'the battle of the nations' in which the Muslims faced the confederates?
questions.explanation: The Trench battle is also called Ghazwah al-Ahzab, the battle of the confederates.

questions.prompt: How many Muslims were at the Battle of Badr compared to the Quraysh?
questions.explanation: Roughly 313 Muslims faced about 1,000 Quraysh at Badr.
